Subject: Mandatory Declassification Review (MDR) Request under Executive Order 13526 — Withheld Exhibits, Segregated Records, and Classified Malta Testimony from the U.S. Navy Court of Inquiry into the USS Liberty (AGTR-5)

Dear MDR Coordinator:

I am a survivor of the June 8, 1967, Israeli attack on the USS Liberty and serve my shipmates as Vice President and Historian of the USS Liberty Veterans Association (https://ussliberty.org)

Pursuant to Section 3.5 of Executive Order 13526 and 32 C.F.R. § 2001.33, I formally request a Mandatory Declassification Review of all classified, withheld, or redacted records associated with the U.S. Navy Court of Inquiry convened in June 1967 to investigate the armed attack on the USS Liberty (AGTR-5).

Specific Records Requested
The target records reside primarily within Record Group 125 (Records of the Office of the Judge Advocate General, Navy) and Record Group 38 (Records of the Chief of Naval Operations) at the National Archives at College Park, Maryland:

1.	Classified & Withheld Exhibits of the Record of Proceedings:

o	All exhibits submitted to the Court of Inquiry convened by Commander in Chief, U.S. Naval Forces, Europe (CINCUSNAVEUR) under Rear Admiral Isaac C. Kidd, Jr., USN, that were redacted, classified "Top Secret" / "Secret," or excluded from the public declassification of the Record of Proceedings.
o	Specific investigative exhibits including radar and navigation plots, ship track charts, intercept logs, damage control diagrams, ordnance fragment analyses, and raw photographic evidence collected aboard the ship or submitted to the Court in Malta.

2.	Malta Testimony and Depositions:

o	The complete, unredacted transcripts, sworn statements, and verbatim depositions taken by Rear Admiral Isaac C. Kidd, Jr. and the Court from surviving officers, crew members, and technical research personnel in Valletta, Malta, between June 10 and June 18, 1967, including any transcripts marked "Top Secret" and maintained in segregated files outside the main public volume.
o	Verbatim testimony, statements, and exhibits submitted by Communications Technician (CT) personnel assigned to the Naval Security Group Command (NAVSECGRU) detachment aboard USS Liberty.

3.	Endorsements and Administrative Review Records:

o	The complete, unredacted endorsement, commentary, and forwarding correspondence prepared by Admiral John S. McCain Jr., USN, Commander in Chief, U.S. Atlantic Fleet (CINCLANTFLT), forwarding the findings of the Court of Inquiry.
o	Any concurring, dissenting, or supplementary memoranda prepared by members of the Court, staff legal officers, or convening authorities accompanying the record to the Judge Advocate General of the Navy.

Declassification Standards and Justification
•	Applicability of E.O. 13526 § 3.3 (Automatic Declassification): These records originated in June 1967 and are well over 25 years old. Under Executive Order 13526, historical military operational records of this age are subject to automatic declassification unless specifically exempted by an agency head under certified criteria.

•	Obsolescence of Tactical/Cryptologic Sensitivities: Tactical fleet maneuvers, damage control findings, radar logs, and historical testimony from 1967 possess zero current operational military sensitivity. Declassification cannot reveal active intelligence methods, cryptographic systems, or capabilities of the present-day Armed Forces.

•	Public & Historical Interest: The attack on the USS Liberty remains a matter of significant historical analysis. Public release of the complete, unaltered Record of Proceedings serves the public interest and complies with statutory directives governing historical transparency.

If any specific page or paragraph is determined to meet the exemption criteria of Section 3.3 or Section 6.2 of Executive Order 13526, please segregate and release all non-exempt portions in accordance with Section 3.5(c).

Sincerely,

Joe Meadors
Historian / Member, Board of Directors
Liberty Veterans Association (https://ussliberty.org)

communications.communication:
To Whom It May Concern:

Pursuant to the Connecticut Freedom of Information Act, I hereby request the following records:

This is a request for existing records under the applicable CT public-records law.

Please provide electronic copies of records maintained by UNIFIED SCHOOL DISTRICT 1 from January 1, 2025 through the date of this request concerning the U.S. Department of Education, Office for Civil Rights (OCR) resolution agreement in OCR case 01-22-1129.

I request the following existing records:

1. District correspondence with OCR about the identified agreement or case, including messages to or from OCR-Transition@ed.gov, the OCR staff addresses identified in the Agreement or Letter, and other Department of Education addresses ending in @ed.gov when the message concerns this case, agreement, or a related monitoring submission. This includes OCR acknowledgments, feedback, approvals, requests for revision or additional information, closure-related messages, and any bounced, undeliverable, rejected, failed-delivery, out-of-office, automated-reply, non-delivery, or other delivery-status messages, as well as follow-up messages or internal records indicating that an attempted OCR contact or submission did not receive a response. Include attachments and transmittal emails.
2. Records submitted, prepared for submission, or maintained for submission to OCR, including reports, data, policies, training materials, remediation records, implementation updates, requests for approval, transmittal emails, and records identifying deliverables, deadlines, or responsible staff.
3. Internal district emails or memoranda about an inability to reach OCR, delivery failures, unacknowledged submissions, unanswered follow-ups, delayed OCR feedback or approval, delayed submission, or delayed agreement work.

If no responsive records exist, please state that explicitly. If any portion is withheld, please identify the specific exemption and release all reasonably segregable portions. Please provide the records electronically and notify me before incurring fees above $25.

I also request that, if possible and pursuant to Conn. Gen. Stat. § 1-212(d), fees be waived as I believe this request is in the public interest and not made for commercial gain. The requested documents will be made available to the public at MuckRock.com.

In the event that there are fees, I would be grateful if you would inform me of the total charges in advance of fulfilling my request. I would prefer the request filled electronically, by e-mail attachment if available or CD-ROM if not.

Thank you in advance for your anticipated cooperation in this matter. I look forward to receiving your response to this request within 4 business days, as the statute requires.

Sincerely,

Neal Morton
